page: Microsoft Azure DC32as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCASv5 family, designed for balanced compute and memory workflows. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. The cache topology includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

System memory totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. The instance has no integrated local storage or attached GPUs, requiring reliance on remote Premium Storage options for persistent disk needs. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates balanced middle-tier results. It records a stress-ng multi-core score of 36,854.76 and a single-core score of 1,994.27. Geekbench testing yields 1,431.0 for single-core execution, 11,581.0 for multi-core throughput, and 22,728.0 in clang compilation tasks. PassMark testing records a CPU mark of 33,782.81, a memory score of 2,268.15, and 12,098.25 in database operations, while in-memory caching benchmarks achieve 31.38 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

Because the DC32as_v5 offers dedicated compute threads with consistent mid-tier benchmark metrics and no local disk overhead, it delivers balanced resource allocation without paying for unused local NVMe volumes. Primary application profiles include mid-tier enterprise software, multi-threaded compilation, continuous integration pipelines, caching layers, and general business applications that utilize networked block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure DC32as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the DCASv5 series, built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 32 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores, supported by 128.0 GB of RAM, which maintains a uniform 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes cryptographic acceleration with AES and SHA-NI, along with standard AVX extensions. The instance provisions no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing networked Premium Storage for disk operations. Benchmark evaluations place it consistently in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 33,782.81, Geekbench multi-core rating of 11,581.0, and 31.38 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware footprint is suitable for enterprise application tiers, build systems, CI/CD runners, and general data processing workloads that do not require dense local solid-state storage.
